The pointwise p_lt_f field is the squared form of p(R,k)<f.

The two hornJohnson fields are the source proof's applications of the general singular-value product comparison cited as [29, Theorem 3.3.16]. They apply only after a squared gain bound for the corresponding displayed block transformation has been proved.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p27_t3_theorem3_2 (data : P27Theorem32Data k q) : (forall i, sigmaMTop i / sqrt(1+f^2*k*q) <= sigmaA i) and (forall j, sigmaC j <= sigmaMTail j * sqrt(1+f^2*k*q))
formal_statement.plain_language: If every combined entry-and-row/column ratio in the strong-RRQR criterion is below f, then all leading singular values of A_k and all trailing singular values of C_k satisfy the two bounds in Theorem 3.2.

informal_proof: Prove a finite-dimensional Cauchy--Schwarz bound for multiplication by A_k inverse B_k. Use it separately for the W_1 and W_2 block transformations, sum the p(R,k)<f inequalities over the k(n-k) pairs, and apply the two cited singular-value product comparisons to derive equations (8) and (9).
informal_statement: Theorem 3.2: p(R,k)<f implies the leading A_k singular-value lower bounds and the trailing C_k singular-value upper bounds with factor sqrt(1+f^2 k(n-k)).

tier_rationale: The proof must reconstruct finite-dimensional matrix-vector Cauchy--Schwarz, two distinct block-transformation gain estimates, the exact aggregation over k(n-k) index pairs, and both indexed singular-value conclusions. This is substantial T2-or-harder work and is not discharged by a Mathlib import. NumStability has no corresponding strong-RRQR or block singular-value theorem, so L receives no material advantage over N.
